intro: To export a presentation as PowerPoint in Keynote on Mac, open the file and choose File > Export To > PowerPoint. Keynote saves a .pptx copy that opens in Microsoft PowerPoint, and your original Keynote file stays unchanged.
tldr: Open the presentation, then choose File > Export To > PowerPoint.
Keynote saves a .pptx copy. Your original Keynote file does not change.
Apple's steps: check the password checkbox, click Save, name the file, pick a Where location, then click Export.
Keynote for iCloud uses More > Download a Copy > PowerPoint instead.
If export shows an error, try the fixes in the troubleshooting list first.

blocks.text: Most people export a deck because someone else needs it. A colleague may run Microsoft PowerPoint. A school may ask for .pptx files. A client may refuse anything that is not Office format. Keynote covers all of these with one menu command. The copy it makes is a normal PowerPoint file, and you can send it the way you send any other file.
Check your Keynote version first

The steps on this page match Apple's export guide, which covers Keynote 15.4 for Mac. Keynote 15.1 arrived on January 28, 2026, as a separate app inside Apple Creator Studio. The older Mac app, version 14.5, no longer gets new features. If your menus look different from the steps below, you may be in a different app or version.
To check the version, open the Keynote menu and choose About Keynote. Write the number down. You need it when you search for a fix or ask someone for help.

items: You saved the deck with ⌘S, so the file on disk matches your last change.
You know which folder the .pptx should go in, so the Where pop-up goes fast.
You know whether the deck has a password. Keynote shows a checkbox for it when it does.
You know who will open the file. PowerPoint is the target app for this export.
You have a copy of the original, in case the export needs a fix later.

blocks.text: Export a presentation as PowerPoint in Keynote on Mac, step by step

Apple's guide gives the path as File > Export To > PowerPoint. Apple lists no keyboard shortcut for Export To, so start from the menu bar. Button labels can shift slightly between Keynote versions. Read each button before you click it, and match the steps to what you see on screen.
What the Require password to open checkbox does

If your original deck has a password, the export sheet shows a checkbox labelled Require password to open. Apple's steps say this checkbox appears when the original has a password. Read the label before you click Export, and choose the setting that fits who will open the file.

A password you forget is hard to get back. Keep it in a password manager or somewhere you will find it, and tell the recipient how to open the file. Do not put the password in the file name, because anyone who sees the name can read it.
Keep the original Keynote file safe

Export does not change the source file. Apple's guide says the original is unchanged, so you can export as often as you need. Many people still duplicate the deck before a large edit. Press ⇧⌘S to Duplicate, or press ⌥⇧⌘S to Save As when you want a new name and a new location.

blocks.text: Apple's shortcut list can change with each release. If a shortcut does not respond, find the same action in the menu bar and use the menu.
Export from Keynote for iCloud in a browser

Keynote for iCloud runs in a browser, so the export path is different. Apple's page says to open More, choose Download a Copy, then choose PowerPoint. The file saves to the download location your browser uses. Check your browser's downloads list when the file finishes.

items: Open the presentation in Keynote for iCloud.
Choose Download a Copy, then PowerPoint.
Open the downloaded .pptx in Microsoft PowerPoint and check the slides.

blocks.text: Some third-party guides call this item Send a copy. Apple's wording is Download a Copy, so search for that exact phrase if your screen shows something else.
Creator Studio, Keynote 15.1, and what it costs

Apple moved Keynote into Creator Studio with version 15.1. MacRumors reports that Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year in the U.S. Check Apple's pricing before you subscribe, because prices can change.
Apple's Creator Studio features page says Keynote collaboration files can be up to 4GB. If your deck is large, check its file size in Finder before you send it to anyone.
Fix the error 'There was an error accessing' during export

Some people see 'There was an error accessing' followed by a file path when they export. An older Apple Community thread describes this error in Keynote 5.0.5. That version is far older than the app you use today, so treat its fixes as a starting point, not a guarantee.

items: Copy the slides into a new Keynote document, then export the new document.
Convert CMYK images to RGB, then place them back into the deck.
Ungroup grouped objects, then export again.
If you do not need to edit the file in PowerPoint, export a PDF instead.

blocks.text: Try the fixes in that order. Start with the copy into a new document, since it takes the least effort. Keep the original deck untouched while you test, so you can compare the results.
A worked example: sending a deck to a client on Windows

Say you built a pitch in Keynote and the client uses Microsoft PowerPoint on Windows. Save the deck first with ⌘S. Then choose File > Export To > PowerPoint and name the file after the client, not after your draft. Keep the file in a folder on your Mac, then attach the .pptx to your email.

Open the file once in PowerPoint before you send it. Look for slides that changed shape or lost a font. Fix the original in Keynote, export again, and replace the attachment. Tell the client which slides changed, so they do not compare the versions alone.
Common mistakes people make with this export

The most common mistake is exporting too early. If you export, then edit the deck, the .pptx no longer matches your Keynote file. Export after your final pass, or export again after every change that matters.

The second mistake is editing the .pptx and then trying to bring those edits back into Keynote. You end up with two versions to track. Pick one file as the master, and treat the other one as an export.
Check the .pptx in Microsoft PowerPoint

Open the .pptx in Microsoft PowerPoint and click through every slide. Look at the title slide, any charts, and slides with photos or custom fonts. Check that text still fits inside its boxes, because spacing can shift between apps.
If a slide looks wrong, go back to the Keynote deck and fix the original. Then export again. Do not patch every copy by hand, or the versions drift apart.
Which export path to use

Use File > Export To > PowerPoint when you work in the Keynote app on your Mac and need a .pptx. Use More > Download a Copy > PowerPoint when you work in Keynote for iCloud. Use PDF when the reader only views the slides and never edits them.
How common PowerPoint files are

PowerPoint is still a common format. An Acuity Training survey from March 2023 asked 2,011 UK adults aged 16 and over about presentations. The survey estimates that more than 20.3 million people in the UK have used PowerPoint. That figure is an extrapolation from a training company's survey, not a census count.
The same survey reports that 53% of UK people have been required to create presentations at work or in personal life. Expect a PowerPoint request now and then, and keep these export steps close.
What to do after you export

Send the .pptx with a short note about what changed. If the deck uses speaker notes, check that they came through in PowerPoint before you send it. For more on notes in Keynote, read [How to add presenter notes keynote mac: step by step for Keynote 15.4 and macOS 26](/how-to/add-presenter-notes-in-keynote).

If you need a video of the deck instead, the steps are different. See [How to export keynote presentation movie mac: a Keynote 15.4 guide for macOS 26](/how-to/export-a-presentation-as-a-movie-in-keynote). Teachers who share lesson decks can also read [Keynote for teachers on Mac: lesson slides, presenter view and themes in Keynote 15.3](/for/teachers/keynote).

faq.question: Does Keynote export a .ppt or a .pptx file?
faq.answer: Apple's export guide says Keynote saves the file as .pptx, which opens in Microsoft PowerPoint. If a recipient asks for an older .ppt file, check what their version of PowerPoint accepts before you export.

faq.question: Where is Export To in Keynote on Mac?
faq.answer: Open the File menu, hover over Export To, then choose PowerPoint. Apple lists no keyboard shortcut for Export To, so use the menu.

faq.question: Does exporting change my Keynote file?
faq.answer: No. Apple's guide says the original is unchanged. The .pptx is a separate file, so edits you make in PowerPoint do not flow back into the Keynote deck.

faq.question: Why don't I see the password checkbox?
faq.answer: Apple's steps say the Require password to open checkbox appears when the original file has a password. If your deck has no password, the checkbox does not show.

faq.question: Can I export to PowerPoint from Keynote for iCloud?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose More > Download a Copy > PowerPoint. The file saves to your browser's download location.

faq.question: What does 'There was an error accessing' mean?
faq.answer: It is an export error that shows a file path. An older Apple Community thread about Keynote 5.0.5 lists fixes. Those fixes may not match current Keynote, so test them on a copy of the deck.

faq.question: How much does Keynote cost?
faq.answer: MacRumors reports that Apple Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year in the U.S., and Keynote is part of it. Check Apple's pricing before you buy, because prices can change.

task: Export a Keynote presentation as a PowerPoint file
appliesTo: Keynote 15.4 for Mac, and Keynote for iCloud in a browser
requirements: A Mac with Keynote 15.4, the version Apple's export guide covers
Microsoft PowerPoint, if you want to open or edit the .pptx

steps.name: Open the presentation
steps.text: Double-click the .key file in Finder, or open the deck from inside Keynote. Make sure the slides you want are the ones on screen before you export.

steps.name: Save your latest edits
steps.text: Press ⌘S so the file on disk matches what you see. This takes a moment and protects your last changes.

steps.name: Open the Export To submenu
steps.text: Click File in the menu bar. Hover over Export To, then choose PowerPoint.
steps.tip: Apple lists no keyboard shortcut for Export To, so the menu is the path.

steps.name: Read the password checkbox
steps.text: If the original deck has a password, a checkbox labelled Require password to open appears. Decide whether the .pptx should keep that requirement, then tick or clear the box to match.

steps.name: Click Save
steps.text: Click Save in the sheet. Button names can shift between versions, so read the button before you click it. Keynote then asks for a name and a location.

steps.name: Name the file
steps.text: Type a name in the name field. Keynote saves the copy as a .pptx file, and your original Keynote file stays where it is.

steps.name: Add tags if you use them
steps.text: Tags are optional. Add them only if you sort your files with tags on the Mac. Skip this step if you do not.
steps.tip: Tags help only if you already use them for other files.

steps.name: Pick a location
steps.text: Open the Where pop-up and choose a folder. Pick the same folder as your deck if you want the two files side by side.

steps.name: Click Export
steps.text: Click Export to write the .pptx. When it finishes, open the file in Microsoft PowerPoint and check each slide.
steps.tip: If you see an error with a file path, read the troubleshooting list before you try again.

shortcuts.action: Save As, with a new name or location

troubleshooting.problem: Export fails with 'There was an error accessing' and a file path
troubleshooting.fix: Copy the slides into a new Keynote document and export that. If you do not need edits, export a PDF instead. Test each fix on a copy of the deck.

troubleshooting.problem: No password checkbox in the export sheet
troubleshooting.fix: The Require password to open checkbox appears when the original has a password. If your deck has none, the checkbox will not show.

troubleshooting.problem: Export To is missing from the File menu
troubleshooting.fix: Check your version in the Keynote menu. Keynote 15.1 moved into a separate Creator Studio app, and the older 14.5 app no longer gets new features.

troubleshooting.problem: Keynote for iCloud has no Export To item
troubleshooting.fix: Use More > Download a Copy > PowerPoint. The file goes to your browser's download location.
Convert CMYK images to RGB before you export. The older Apple Community thread reports this fix.

troubleshooting.problem: The .pptx does not match your Keynote slides
troubleshooting.fix: Open it in Microsoft PowerPoint and check each slide. Fix the original in Keynote, then export again rather than editing every copy.
